purpose: Formalize dividend/payout sustainability as a non-monotone fundamental validation state rather than a high-yield or high-payout buy signal.

lifecycle.positiveMechanism: Mature profitable firms with accumulated earned equity and fewer high-return reinvestment opportunities can rationally distribute a larger fraction of internally generated capital.
countermechanisms: high payout can reflect weak growth opportunities rather than superior quality
low payout can reflect valuable reinvestment rather than shareholder hostility
young/high-growth firms may prefer stock distributions or retention
mature firms can overdistribute if governance incentives or investor demand dominate fundamentals

earningsCoverage.positiveMechanism: A cash dividend funded by repeatable earnings has stronger economic support than an equal dividend funded by temporary gains or reserves.
countermechanisms: accounting earnings can be non-cash or low quality
near-zero earnings create unstable payout ratios
cyclical peak earnings can make payout coverage appear safe immediately before normalization

cashCoverage.positiveMechanism: CFO/FCF coverage tests whether cash distributions are supported by operating cash generation after investment needs.
countermechanisms: one-year working-capital release can temporarily inflate CFO
CAPEX can be discretionary/timed and FCF definitions vary
financial institutions do not fit generic industrial FCF semantics

distributionSource.positiveMechanism: Separating current/retained earnings from legal/capital reserve distributions prevents stable cash payout from being mistaken for stable current earning power.
countermechanisms: reserve-funded cash can be legally valid and economically sensible
reserve distribution may support payout stability through a temporary downturn
the same nominal DPS can have very different sustainability depending on source

payoutAlternatives.positiveMechanism: Dividends are only one shareholder-payout mechanism; repurchases and cash capital reductions can substitute for dividends.
countermechanisms: comparing dividend payout alone can misclassify firms using alternative payout methods
tax/clientele effects can change the chosen payout form without changing core operating quality
payoutAlternatives.antiDoubleCount: Alternative payout events are dependent context from their canonical owners and cannot become duplicate independent votes.

lifecycleStudy.citation: Wang, Ke, Liu & Huang (2011), Dividend Policy and the Life Cycle Hypothesis: Evidence from Taiwan
lifecycleStudy.sample: 6031 dividend-payment observations, 1992-2007, Taiwan Stock Exchange firms
lifecycleStudy.relevance: Supports heterogeneous cash-vs-stock dividend behavior across profitability/growth/lifecycle states.
lifecycleStudy.importRule: Mechanism evidence only; historical coefficients are not imported as current Taiwan alpha.

taxImputationStudy.citation: Chan & Lin (2017), Imputation tax system, dividend payout, and investor behavior: Evidence from the Taiwan stock exchange
taxImputationStudy.relevance: Taiwan tax regime changed cash-dividend payout and investor behavior, demonstrating that payout policy is partly institutional/clientele-driven rather than pure operating quality.
taxImputationStudy.importRule: Tax-era findings are context evidence; current strategy requires current-law/PIT treatment.

dividendClienteleStudy.citation: Lee, Liu, Roll & Subrahmanyam (2006), Taxes and dividend clientele: Evidence from trading and ownership structure
dividendClienteleStudy.relevance: Investor tax heterogeneity affected dividend holdings/trading and later repurchase propensity in Taiwan.
dividendClienteleStudy.importRule: Confirms clientele mechanism; does not imply direction for future stock returns.

capitalReserveEvidence.citation: Pacific Accounting Review (2022), cash dividends from capital reserves and governance in Taiwan
capitalReserveEvidence.relevance: Shows Taiwan reserve-funded cash distributions are economically distinct from earnings-funded ordinary dividends.
capitalReserveEvidence.importRule: Distribution source must be preserved; reserve-funded cash is not automatically bad or ordinary earnings payout.

universalHighPayout: Reject if apparent quality disappears after controlling for profitability, growth opportunities, retained-earnings maturity, leverage and sector.
Reject if high payout is concentrated in declining-growth or weak-reinvestment firms without superior future operating quality.
stableDividendEqualsSustainable: Reject if stable DPS is maintained through reserve distributions, rising leverage or declining cash coverage.
Reject if ordinary payout sequence becomes unstable once special/reserve-funded cash is removed.
lowPayoutEqualsBadShareholderPolicy: Reject if retained cash is followed by high incremental ROIC, profitable growth or value-creating investment.
Treat buybacks/cash-capital-reductions as alternative payout context rather than dividend omission.
highYieldEqualsSafety: Reject as a fundamental rule because dividend yield can rise mechanically when price collapses.
Dividend yield remains D08 valuation context and is not a D07-34 sustainability score.

decisionRole.hardInvalidation: NONE by default; only source/identity invalidity may hard-block the metric itself.

antiDoubleCount: D07-02 owns raw earnings; D07-34 uses earnings only as payout coverage denominator.
D07-05 owns CFO/FCF quality; D07-34 uses it only for payout funding coverage.
D07-06 owns leverage/liquidity; D07-34 uses it only as sustainability constraint.
D08 owns dividend yield/valuation; D07-34 never converts price yield into fundamental quality.
D11 owns ex-date/payment mechanics; D07-34 consumes event clocks for PIT alignment only.
D21 owns governance/capital-allocation process; D07-34 owns economic/accounting capacity.

sourceStatus.l3Gate: Requires a clean Taiwan PIT/replay receipt with proposal/final/version chronology and denominator alignment.

maturityAssessment.reason: Mechanism, countermechanisms, falsification, decision role and anti-double-count ownership are now explicitly defined with Taiwan-specific evidence. L3 remains blocked because historical PIT replay of dividend decision/source/vintage chronology is not yet physically validated.
